"Beats the type's average deviation" means strictly greater than, so pairs equal to the average are dropped. The alternative is greater than or equal to, which keeps pairs equal to the average with an excess of zero.
"Beats" means a lower deviation than the type's average, meaning pairs closer to the overall average. Excess is then the average deviation minus the pair's deviation.
The type's average deviation is computed over all pairs in the type, including those with a missing average. Alternatively, it is computed only over pairs with a non-null deviation.
The type's average deviation is computed over all pairs within the type before filtering. Alternatively, it is the average of the deviations of the type's pairs weighted by snapshot count.

Per tradekind, the output has three averages over the kept pairs: the average pair-level `optvolrt`, the average deviation, and the average excess. Alternatively, the average `optvolrt` is calculated over the raw snapshot rows of the kept pairs, rather than over the pair averages.
The output has one row per `tradekind`, and types with no kept pairs are omitted. Alternatively, such types appear with null averages.

Pairs with a null `tradekind` are excluded from the overall average as well.

Null `optvolrt` values are ignored in each pair average. A pair whose snapshots all have null `optvolrt` has a null average, so its deviation is null and it is dropped. Alternatively, null values are treated as zero.

Pair grouping uses the `transref` of the sentiment snapshot, which is the same as `transreg` after the join. It could instead be read as grouping by each individual sentiment snapshot (`sentreg`), where a snapshot is one pair.

The join to the trader uses only `transactionrecord.trdref` = `trader.tradereg`. The alternative is to also use `sentimentandfundamentals.trdref2`, the optional trader reference on the snapshot, as the trader link.

The same as 1, but the "overall average" is computed within each trader type (the average `optvolrt` across the joined snapshots of that `tradekind`), not across all trader types, so each pair's deviation is measured from its own type's average.
queries:
WITH joined AS (
  SELECT s.transref AS transref, t.tradekind AS tradekind, s.optvolrt AS optvolrt
  FROM sentimentandfundamentals s
  JOIN transactionrecord r ON s.transref = r.transreg
  JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(optvolrt) AS overall_avg FROM joined
),
pairs AS (
  SELECT transref, tradekind, AVG(optvolrt) - (SELECT overall_avg FROM overall) AS deviation
  FROM joined
  GROUP BY transref, tradekind
),
typed AS (
  SELECT transref, tradekind, deviation,
         AVG(deviation) OVER (PARTITION BY tradekind) AS type_avg_dev
  FROM pairs
)
SELECT transref, tradekind, deviation, deviation - type_avg_dev AS excess
FROM typed
WHERE deviation > type_avg_dev;
SELECT t.tradekind, AVG(s.infoleaksc) AS avg_infoleaksc, (SELECT AVG(infoleaksc) FROM sentimentandfundamentals) AS overall_avg_infoleaksc
FROM sentimentandfundamentals s
JOIN transactionrecord tr ON s.transref = tr.transreg
JOIN trader t ON tr.trdref = t.tradereg
GROUP BY t.tradekind;
WITH pair_avg AS (
  SELECT tradekind, posspan, AVG(acctbal) AS pair_avg
  FROM trader
  GROUP BY tradekind, posspan
),
type_avg AS (
  SELECT tradekind, AVG(acctbal) AS overall_avg
  FROM trader
  GROUP BY tradekind
),
dev AS (
  SELECT p.tradekind, p.posspan, ABS(p.pair_avg - t.overall_avg) AS abs_dev
  FROM pair_avg p
  JOIN type_avg t ON p.tradekind = t.tradekind
),
type_dev AS (
  SELECT tradekind, AVG(abs_dev) AS avg_abs_dev
  FROM dev
  GROUP BY tradekind
)
SELECT d.tradekind, d.posspan, d.abs_dev - td.avg_abs_dev AS excess
FROM dev d
JOIN type_dev td ON d.tradekind = td.tradekind
WHERE d.abs_dev > td.avg_abs_dev;
SELECT tradekind,
       AVG(acctbal) AS avg_acctbal,
       (AVG(acctbal) - (SELECT AVG(acctbal) FROM trader)) * 100.0 / (SELECT AVG(acctbal) FROM trader) AS pct_deviation
FROM trader
GROUP BY tradekind;
